newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed, NYH gains on weather, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed, NYH gains on weather, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed again Monday in moderate, late trade, with New York grades gaining in the face of the season's first heat wave, while Gulf Coast values were steady to down slightly.

"Florida and East Coast utilities have to be burning this week and with oil more competitive with gas, I think we're going higher from here," said one cash trader, noting hot East Coast weather was expected to last at least through the week.
In New York Harbor, low sulphur utility interest again firmed physical one percent prices slightly to $16.00-25 a barrel, with July paper up more than a quarter to $16.10-30.
NYH August one percent paper was quoted about even to July, with September pegged about 10 cents under August.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was talked more than 25 cents higher at $17.50-75 amid prospects for better cooling demand and still-limited supply.
High sulphurs in New York were 10-20 cents higher, with 2.2 percent now seen at $14.50-75 after a 100,000 barrel prompt deal reported late Friday at $14.75.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent held at $15.75, while three percent notionally was steady at $13.50-75, traders said.

New York city gate swing gas prices jumped almost a dime on the heat to the high-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $16.25 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained a nickel to about $2.29/mmBtu, or $14.43 a barrel.
